questions.markdown:
Given points $A(2,5,-1)$, $B(3,-2,4)$ and $C(-2,3,1)$. Find:

(i) $\vec{R}_{AB} \cdot \vec{R}_{AC}$

(ii) The angle between $\vec{R}_{AB}$ and $\vec{R}_{AC}$

(iii) The length of the projection of $\vec{R}_{AB}$ on $\vec{R}_{AC}$

(iv) The vector projection of $\vec{R}_{AB}$ on $\vec{R}_{AC}$

Transform each of the following vectors to cylindrical coordinates at the specified point:

(i) $5\,\mathbf{a}_x$ at $P\, (\rho = 4,\, \phi = 120^\circ,\, z=-1)$

(ii) $5\,\mathbf{a}_x$ at $Q\, (x=3,\, y=4,\, z=-1)$

(iii) $4\,\mathbf{a}_x - 2\,\mathbf{a}_y - 4\,\mathbf{a}_z$ at $R\, (x=2,\, y=3,\, z=5)$

An infinitely long uniform line charge is located at $y=3,\, z=5$. If $\rho_L = 30\ \text{nC/m}$, find electric field intensity at

(i) The origin

(ii) At $P\,(0,6,1)$

Within the sphere $r=1\ \text{m}$, the electric potential is given as $V = 10 + 10r^2 + \sin\theta + \cos\phi\ (\text{V})$. Find the following at $P\,(r=1,\, \theta=\pi/2,\, \phi=0)$:

(i) Electric potential

(ii) Electric field intensity

(iii) Electric flux density

(iv) Volume charge density

(v) The charge that lies within the sphere $r=1\ \text{m}$.

Inside a cylindrical region, $\rho \le 4\ (\text{m})$, the electric flux density is given as $\mathbf{D} = 5\rho^2\, \mathbf{a}_\rho\ (\text{C/m}^2)$. Find:

(i) The volume charge density at $\rho = 3\ (\text{m})$

(ii) The electric flux density at $\rho = 3\ (\text{m})$

(iii) The electric flux that leaves the cylinder $\rho = 3,\ |z|\le 2.5$

questions.markdown: State and prove Gauss Divergence Theorem.

Let a filamentary current of 5 mA be directed from infinity to the origin on the positive $z$ axis and then back out to infinity on the positive $x$ axis. Find magnetic field intensity $\mathbf{H}$ at $P\,(0,1,0)$.

If vector magnetic potential $\mathbf{A} = 10\rho^{1.5}\, \mathbf{a}_z\ \text{Wb/m}$ in free space, find:

(i) Magnetic field intensity $\mathbf{H}$

(ii) Current density $\mathbf{J}$

(iii) Prove Ampere’s Circuital Law for a circular path with $\rho = 1$.
Derive the boundary conditions of static magnetic field at the interface of two different magnetic medium.

A lossy dielectric has an intrinsic impedance of $200\angle 30^\circ\ \Omega$ at a particular radian frequency $\omega$. If, at that frequency, the plane wave propagating through the dielectric has the magnetic field component

$$
\mathbf{H} = 10 e^{-\alpha x}\cos\left(\omega t - \tfrac{1}{2}x\right)\,\mathbf{y}\ \text{A/m},
$$

find $\mathbf{E}$ and $\alpha$.

questions.markdown: In a non-magnetic medium $\mathbf{E} = 4\sin(2\pi\times 10^7 t - 0.8x)\,\mathbf{z}\ \text{V/m}$. Find (a) $\epsilon_r$, $\eta$, (b) The time average power carried by the wave.
The electric field in free-space is given by $\mathbf{E}(z,t) = E_0^+\cos(2\pi\times 10^6 t - \beta z)$. Using Maxwell's equations, find the magnetic field $\mathbf{H}$.
A distortionless line has $Z_0 = 60\ \Omega$, $\alpha = 20\ \text{mNp/m}$, $u = 0.6c$, where $c$ is the speed of light in a vacuum. Find $R$, $L$, $G$, $C$, and $\lambda$ at 100 MHz.

A lossless transmission line with $Z_0=50\ \Omega$ is 30 m long and operates at 2 MHz. The line is terminated with a load $Z_L = 60 + j40\ \Omega$. If velocity of wave = $0.6c$ on the line, find, (i) the reflection coefficient, (ii) the standing wave ratio, (iii) the input impedance. Where $c$ is velocity of light.
